subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call instead?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the issue touches sandboxed shell execution semantics and the report explicitly allows either a compatibility-preserving warning or a stricter failure.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so the user must opt into a different host or elevated path.

options.title: Defer To Fork PR Review
options.body: Review and possibly adopt the open fork PR only after deciding whether warning-only behavior is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history signal for original PTY support, fallback behavior, and adjacent exec docs/runtime decisions.
